title: Wait for God to Say Go

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: By the twenty-seventh day of the second month the earth was completely dry. Then God said to Noah, "Come out of the ark, you and your wife and your sons and their wives." - Gen 8:14-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the confirmation of Noah's patience. Even after he saw the dry ground, he stayed in the ark - nearly two more months - until God said the words: "Come out of the ark." Noah waited for God's command before he moved. He would not leave until the God who told him to go in told him to come out.

Think about the discipline this required. The ground was dry. The door could be opened. Everything in Noah must have longed to be free of that ark after more than a year inside. Yet he waited on the word of God. He had entered at God's command, and he would leave at God's command. His whole life was ordered by the voice of the Lord.

This is a beautiful model of a life surrendered to God. Noah did not act on his own impulses or even on the plain evidence before his eyes. He listened for God's word and let it govern his steps - when to go in, when to come out, when to move, when to wait.

What a difference it makes to live this way! So much heartache comes from moving without waiting for God, from opening doors He has not opened for us. The path of blessing is to let God set the pace: "in all your ways submit to him, and he will make your paths straight" (Prov 3:6). Wait for God to say "go," and you will never move too soon.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you ordering your steps by God's word, or by your own impulses?
- Is there a decision where you need to wait for God's clear "go"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, order my steps by Your word, as Noah's were. Give me the patience to wait for Your "go," and the trust to move only when You lead. Let Your voice govern my life.
